    ====Verb==== wow (third-person singular simple present [[:wows#English|wows]], present participle [[:wowing#English|wowing]], simple past and past participle [[:wowed#English|wowed]])[[Category:English lemmas|WOW]][[Category:English verbs|WOW]][[Category:English palindromes|WOW]][[Category:English entries with incorrect language header|WOW]][[Category:Pages with entries|WOW]][[Category:Pages with 12 entries|WOW]] # ([[Appendix:Glossary#transitive|transitive]][[Category:English transitive verbs|WOW]], [[Appendix:Glossary#informal|informal]][[Category:English informal terms|WOW]]) To [[amaze]] or [[awe]]. #:
    He really '''wowed''' the audience.

    '''2015''', Joe Sweeney, Mike Yorkey, Moving the Needle, John Wiley & Sons, [[Special:BookSources/978-1-118-94410-3|→ISBN]], [https://books.google.com/books?id=k3AgBQAAQBAJ&pg=PA200&dq=%22wowed%22&hl=&cd=8&source=gbs_api#v=onepage&q=%22wowed%22&f=false page 200]:[[Category:English terms with quotations|WOW]]
    If all of us can remember how great it felt to be '''wowed''', why don't we make it a habit to do it more often for others? People remember you when you '''wow''' them, so to differentiate yourself with your clients and customers, think of doing something that would make them remember you.
    [[Category:English terms with quotations|WOW]]
    #*
    '''2023''' May 8, Nesrine Malik, “The coronation pulled a screen across a desperate, failing nation – just as intended”, in [[:w:Katharine Viner|Katharine Viner]], editor, [[:w:The Guardian|The Guardian]]‎[https://web.archive.org/web/20261019124202/https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2023/may/08/coronation-desperate-nation-rotten-system], London: [[:w:Guardian Media Group|Guardian News & Media]], [https://www.worldcat.org/issn/0261-3077 →ISSN], [https://search.worldcat.org/title/229952407 →OCLC], archived from [https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2023/may/08/coronation-desperate-nation-rotten-system the original] on 19 October 2026:[[Category:English terms with quotations|WOW]]
